transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate your time. 

Um... well, I suppose I'm here because things got a little out of hand recently, though I really was just trying to be helpful. I hope it's okay if I just start with that? 

I took on this project for the local historical society, and... well, I guess I sort of acted like I could run the entire fundraiser all by myself. I just got so inspired to do a good job for them. I started drawing up all these new quilt designs, and I was calling all the volunteers, making these big elaborate schedules for everyone... I just wanted it to be perfect, you know? 

But, um, I ended up promising people all these deadlines that I... well, that I couldn't possibly meet. I feel a little silly about it now, to be honest. I just wanted to be useful. Does that make sense as a reason to be here?
Can you tell me more about how you were feeling during that time with the fundraiser? Were you feeling more energetic, unusually confident, or like your thoughts were racing?

Well... yes, energetic, I suppose. I mean, at first, it was lovely. I felt almost... glowing, if that doesn't sound too strange? Like every single idea I had was just wonderful and I was finally doing something truly worthwhile. I felt so capable, and I thought I was being so helpful. 

But... well, I have to admit, and I feel just awful about this... if anyone questioned my plans, or told me maybe we didn't need fifty custom quilts in a week... I got a little, um, snappish. Which isn't like me at all! I just felt like they were standing in the way of this beautiful thing I was trying to build. I wasn't trying to be difficult, I promise. I just wanted it to be right. Does that sound like what you mean?
How long did you feel this way — this increased energy, confidence, and rush of ideas — during the time with the fundraiser?

Oh, well... let me think. I hope I'm remembering this right, I don't want to give you the wrong information. 

It felt like it went on for quite a while, actually. I'd say that whole stretch—where I was just working so hard on the project and feeling so... driven—lasted for about five months. Yes, almost half the year, really, before I just couldn't keep up with it anymore and everything sort of... fell apart. 

I know five months is a long time to be acting like that. I really should have realized sooner that I was taking on too much, shouldn't I? I just got so caught up in wanting to be helpful. I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for?
During that time you felt so driven and full of ideas, was there a period where your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

Oh, um... a whole week? Like, every single day, most of the day? I'm... I'm really not sure, to be perfectly honest. I hope it's alright that my memory is a little fuzzy on the exact days. 

It mostly just felt like a long, steady stretch of being very focused on the quilts. I don't think I was unusually... high or overly excited the entire time, just very busy and determined, you know? And the irritability... well, I really try my best to be polite, so I certainly hope I wasn't snapping at people every day for a whole week. That sounds just dreadful of me, and I'd hate for anyone to think I behaved that poorly for that long. 

I mostly just remember that general drive to get things done over those months, rather than one specific week where it was all happening at once. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful... is it okay that I can't pinpoint a specific week like that for you?
Can you recall if there was a time during those five months when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least one full week?

Oh, I see. I'm so sorry, I must not have answered you properly a moment ago. Um... well, if I really think back to the very beginning of it all... like I was saying earlier, there was that initial stretch where I felt just... glowing. Where it seemed like every idea I had was just brilliant. 

And I suppose... well, yes, if I'm being completely honest, that intense feeling, and then getting so terribly snappish when the other ladies questioned me... acting like they were standing in the way of my plans... that probably did happen every day for at least a week or two when we first got started. I just didn't want to admit it because I feel so ashamed that I was that difficult for that many days in a row. I really do try to be a cooperative person, I promise. 

Does that help answer your question better? I hope I'm giving you what you need this time.
During that initial intense period when you felt very driven and irritable, was there a time when your mood was elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least one full week?

Oh, um... yes, I think we... we just went over that, didn't we? I'm so sorry, I hope I wasn't being confusing before. 

But yes, like I said, at first I felt almost... glowing. It was like every idea I had was just wonderful. But then... well, if anyone questioned me, I got terribly snappish. I acted like they were standing in the way of everything I was trying to do. And that did go on for at least a week or two, most of the day, every day. 

I really am so embarrassed about how I acted toward those ladies. I hope you don't think I'm normally that sort of person? I'm usually very easy to get along with, I promise. Did I answer it right this time?

During that same time when you felt very driven and irritable, did you also experience things like needing less sleep, talking more quickly than usual, having thoughts race from one idea to the next, being easily distracted, or engaging in activities that could have risky consequences?

Oh, um... well, there's quite a bit in that question, isn't there? I'll try to answer as best I can, I promise. 

As for the sleep... well, I suppose my sleep schedule did get a little bit... unusual during that time. For a while there, I was only sleeping a few hours a night. But I wasn't tired! I'd wake up feeling just perfectly refreshed and ready to start sewing or making phone calls for the project. I hope it's alright that I was making calls so early... I just felt so productive, you know? 

But lately, things have changed. Now I find myself just lying awake in bed, worrying about everything, or... or I'll sleep in quite late and still feel completely worn out when I finally do get up. It's very frustrating, and I hate being so lazy in the mornings now. 

I'm not so sure about the racing thoughts or the risky activities... I really try to be careful and sensible. Did I explain the sleep part well enough for you? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.

During that same time when you felt very driven and irritable, did you notice your thoughts moving very quickly from one idea to the next, or did you find yourself talking more than usual, perhaps even feeling like you couldn't stop?

Oh, well... I suppose my mind was quite busy during those weeks. I really hope I didn't talk people's ears off, because I always try to be a polite listener, I truly do. 

But... um, if I'm looking back on it honestly, yes, my thoughts did seem to be moving terribly fast. I just had so much I wanted to accomplish, you see. My mind would just race from the quilt blocks we were working on, right over to the donor lists, and then suddenly I'd be thinking about the Sunday church announcements. It was all moving so quickly that I just couldn't hold onto one single thought long enough to actually finish it before the next one popped up. 

I feel a bit foolish admitting how scatterbrained I was being. It sounds so disorganized, and I'm usually a very focused person, I promise. Is that what you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.

During that time when you felt so driven and your thoughts were racing, did you find yourself doing things that could have had serious consequences, like spending a lot of money, taking on too many responsibilities, or making big decisions without thinking them through?

Oh, goodness... well, I really hope I didn't do anything too terrible. I'm usually so careful with money, and I'd never want to make a rash decision that would hurt anyone. 

But... um, I suppose I did take on rather a lot of responsibility. More than was sensible, looking back. That's actually sort of what brings me in, if I'm being perfectly honest. I... well, I took on the historical society project, and I just acted like I could run the whole fundraiser all by myself. I started drawing up all these quilt designs, and I was calling volunteers at all hours, making these elaborate schedules... 

I even promised everyone these deadlines that, well, I couldn't possibly meet. I just felt so capable at the time, like I could handle absolutely anything. I feel just awful about it now, letting people down like that. It's really not like me to overpromise, I try so hard to be reliable. Does... does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm completely irresponsible.

Can you confirm if there was at least one full week when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like feeling unusually high, overly confident, or irritable—nearly every day and most of the day, not just moments here and there?

Oh, well... yes, I suppose it was at least a week. Probably a bit longer, actually. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it was, but... yes, it was every day for a while there. 

At first, I just felt... oh, almost glowing, if that makes sense? I felt so wonderful, and every single idea I had for the fundraiser just seemed absolutely brilliant. I felt so capable and full of energy. But... well, I feel terrible admitting this, because I really do try to be kind to everyone... if anyone questioned my plans or suggested we slow down, I got awfully snappish with them. I just felt like they were standing in the way of all this important work we had to do. 

I'm usually much more patient, I promise I am. I just... I couldn't seem to help being a bit short-tempered when they didn't see my vision. Is that the sort of thing you're looking for? I hope I'm explaining it properly for you.

Can you confirm if there was a specific period lasting at least one full week when your mood was clearly elevated, overly confident, or irritable, most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just occasional moments?

Oh, dear, I must not have explained myself very well just a moment ago. I'm so sorry to make you ask again! Yes, it was certainly at least a week. In fact... well, if I'm being completely honest, it was quite a bit longer than that. 

I feel a little silly admitting just how long I was acting that way, but... that whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project? It actually went on for about five months. Five whole months of feeling that way, day in and day out, before... well, before everything just sort of fell apart on me. 

I hope I didn't confuse you earlier by not being specific enough. Does that give you a better picture of what happened? I really do want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
